title: Does the viewer protocol keep messages and fields no client reads?
body:
The viewer protocol is unreleased: v0.1.0 has no `docs/viewer.md`. These parts of `wire.rs` have no reader today.

| item | sender | reader |
|---|---|---|
| `Output`, `Workspaces`, `Showing` | the server, on every size change, list change and show | `viewer.rs` drops all three with `=> {}`; `script.rs` and `control::list` with `_ =>` |
| `ViewerMessage::Show` | nobody; only wire tests build it | the server's `show()` is reached from the picker and palette |
| `List` from a welcomed viewer | nobody | a branch in `viewer_message` keeps the viewer connected |
| `CursorImage`, `Cursor` | nobody; `send_cursor` maps `CursorImageStatus::Surface` to `CursorShape("default")` | the viewer maps both to `Shape::Default` |
| `Buffer.opaque` | always `true` | ignored with `..` |
| `Frame.damage` and the `Rect` type | always `Vec::new()` | the viewer damages the whole buffer |
| `Release.fence` | always `None` from both clients | read as `Release { id, .. }` |
| `Formats.device` | the viewer computes `main_device()` and script calls `dev_id()` to send it | read as `Formats { formats, .. }` |
| `Error.code` | both sides | no receiver reads it |
| `Close.reason` | always 1 | the viewer prints a string equal to `message` |
| `PointerLeft` | the viewer | the server handles it with `=> {}` |

The `fenced` flag before `damage` and the fd after it give `Frame` its own encode layout; without damage it is an id plus a fence, like `Release`. Together these are about 300 lines of `wire.rs` and tests plus three doc sections.

## Options

1. Delete everything without a reader now and add it back when a viewer has UI for it. No compatibility cost, the most code removed, and the record of what the protocol was planned to carry goes with it.
2. Keep `Output`, `Workspaces` and `Showing` for a viewer sidebar, and delete the rest. The remote viewer (decade-e3a784) may want them.
3. Keep all of it and only fix the `allow(dead_code)` so the compiler shows what is unused.

I lean to option 2 with `Release.fence` kept, since `docs/viewer.md` argues for the fence on purpose.
close_reason: Landed in 363bbd2 with option 2, keeping the fence in release. The note above lists what went and what stayed.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/913b1d2c
notes.text:
Checked against the code at 49896bf. The table holds: no reader exists for any listed item. `decade-apps` uses only `decade-channel`, never `wire.rs`.

Chose option 2 with `Release.fence` kept. `output`, `workspaces` and `showing` stay for a viewer sidebar and the remote viewer in decade-e3a784. `show` went with the rest, so a viewer cannot pick its workspace over the wire until a viewer has UI for it. `Frame.fence` stays because the server sends a real fence. `Formats.device` went: the server allocates on its own render node and never read it. A multi-GPU host may want it back.

Opcodes were renumbered to stay dense, since the protocol is unreleased and every client ships in the same binary.
